trigger: a maintainer trusts the 4-line comment (and the commit message, which names the same two files) to find the tests that leak into RouteInventory
classification_rationale: The comment's claims are individually true (both named files register on a stack httplib::Server through HttplibRouteSink with no forget) but the attribution is misleading against the tree: the observed 5 is 4 stale routes + the test's own /yuzu_test_forget; only test_health_routes.cpp (4 plain-sink GETs, health_routes.cpp:960-963) and test_step_up_wiring.cpp ApprovalWiringServer (4 routes, approval_routes.cpp:184/231/243/248) register exactly 4; test_settings_routes_ota_audit.cpp registers the full settings set (74 sink call sites) and cannot give 5; test_step_up_wiring.cpp, test_settings_routes_cert_upload.cpp (settings_routes.cpp:2636-2648) and test_scim_routes.cpp (~2880) also leak and are unnamed. Truth call: cpp-expert (verified by reading). Security-guardian labelled SHOULD; derived band is NICE (I9/E0, no operational effect), the derived band governs the gate.
summary: Comment/commit message misattribute the leakers: name the OTA settings test (cannot produce 5), omit test_step_up_wiring.cpp (can). Suggested: 'e.g. test_health_routes.cpp, test_step_up_wiring.cpp' or name no files. Raised independently by security-guardian (sec-F1) and docs-writer (doc-D1) in the Gate 2 wave; echoed by cpp-expert, quality-engineer, consistency-auditor, compliance-officer (C-1). Non-blocking.

trigger: a reader takes 'Without it this REQUIRE intermittently read 5 == 1 in CI' as an established cause; the mechanism was not reproduced (caller: 40 random-order runs, shard B 6/6 passed locally)
classification_rationale: The 5 == 1 reading is observed on two CI legs; that the missing forget caused it is unproven, and the TSan shard-A failure (run 39944539491) is NOT covered because both 4-route leakers are compiled out under TSan. docs-writer owns wording; quality-engineer/cpp-safety own the truth call and made none. Suggested: 'has been seen reading 5 == 1 in CI (dev run 39970288227); stale same-address registration is the suspected cause'.
summary: Unproven causal claim worded as fact, in the comment and in the commit message ('made the REQUIRE read 5 == 1'). CI evidence runs: 39970288227 (dev push, Linux clang-21 debug), 39981762503 (PR #6378, macOS debug), 39944539491 (main, TSan shard A, unconfirmed). Non-blocking.

trigger: the stack slot of `httplib::Server never_registered` (same TEST_CASE, later local than svr) coincides with the address of a destroyed leaker server that left entries in the singleton
classification_rationale: The change protects only svr; the CHECK(routes_for(&never_registered).empty()) in the same test case reads the singleton under a second stack address with no preceding forget, so the same flake can move from the REQUIRE to the CHECK. Pre-existing and less likely than the svr case (different frame offset); not worsened by this diff. One-line fix: RouteInventory::instance().forget(&never_registered); before the check (does not weaken it: an absent key still must read empty). Independently raised in the Gate 2 wave as sec-F2; echoed by architect, cpp-expert, cpp-safety, quality-engineer, consistency-auditor, unhappy-path (UP-1), sre.
summary: `never_registered` is read without a prior forget: residual stale-address exposure in the very test case this commit edits. Recommended fold-in (non-blocking); if folded, Gate 8 must re-run cpp-expert, cpp-safety, quality-engineer, docs-writer (comment edit) against the fix diff.

trigger: the TSan shard-A failure on main run 39944539491 is assumed to be the same bug and the PR/issue is closed or described as fixing it
classification_rationale: Orchestrator verified by grep that both exact-4-route leakers are compiled out under TSan: test_step_up_wiring.cpp:70-1648 sits inside #ifndef YUZU_TSAN_BUILD (defined at :63/:67 under thread_sanitizer) and test_health_routes.cpp:2031-2182 inside #ifndef YUZU_HEALTH_ROUTES_LIVE_TSAN (:73/:77). summary: This fix probably does NOT cover the TSan shard-A failure; do not say it does. Read the assertion and counts in run 39944539491's meson-logs testlog, then decide on a separate issue (chaos CH-3). Needs a terminal disposition (deferred-to-issue after dedupe + filing, or fixed/linked) before merge by superseding row; not filed by this run (read-only constraint).

trigger: any test that registers on a stack httplib::Server through HttplibRouteSink (or a production register_routes(httplib::Server&) overload) and never forgets, followed by any victim whose stack slot matches; also a throwing REQUIRE that skips a trailing forget/seal cleanup
classification_rationale: Five test files / six call sites leak (test_health_routes.cpp:2046, test_settings_routes_ota_audit.cpp:632-635, test_settings_routes_cert_upload.cpp:256-268, test_step_up_wiring.cpp:559-681, test_scim_routes.cpp:2785/2880); the root fix is a scoped RouteInventory guard (forget in ctor and dtor) at those sites, not more victim-side forgets. Architect: do NOT forget in HttplibRouteSink's destructor (production sinks are per-call temporaries, it would empty the boot-sweep input); do not add a clear-all to production for tests. redirect_server_ is never forgotten but nothing reads it (no production consequence). Raised by security-guardian (sec-F3); echoed by architect (g3-3), quality-engineer, cpp-safety, sre, unhappy-path (UP-4).
summary: Follow-up, not a blocker: scoped RouteInventory guard for the leaker fixtures. Needs dedupe probe then file-or-fold; not filed by this run.
